question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
solution:
The correct answer is '**at**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage discusses the rate at which tea imports increased in the Colonies.
 
• The correct preposition to indicate growth or change in rate is "at".
 
• "At a very fast rate" is the standard phrase used to describe something increasing rapidly.
 
• Other options ("beside", "of", "about") do not fit the context or are grammatically incorrect in this phrase.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

 

Complete Passage: *The volume of tea imports into the Colonies rose **at__** a very fast rate in the four years up to the Boston Tea Party. They went from 55 tonnes in 1770, which was close to the amount dumped in the harbour, to 370 tonnes the year the tea was dumped. This was an increase of almost seven times. The population of the Colonies was about 2 million people in 1770 and didn’t change much in that four-year period. Basic economics tells us this sharp increase in supply without more customers meant the price of tea had to fall.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Beside: Means "next to" or "apart from", which does not fit the context of describing the rate of increase.
 
• Of: Does not indicate rate or speed of increase.
 
• About: Used for approximation, not for describing rate or speed.
